solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A university supporting French union member in Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up, so it comes after

explanation.surface: A university is backing a French trade unionist working in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' looks like a trade unionist, but the union is marriage: a wife in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: German for a wife or married woman, one partner in the union of marriage.

clue.text: Marine creature's scent found in most of ocean

indicators.note: the smell sits inside the shortened word, so this marks a container
only most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the sea is another word for the ocean
a pong is a smell, an informal word for an odour

explanation.surface: A sea creature's smell is detected across most of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the ocean word by its last letter; 'found in' signals the container, with 'scent' in the informal sense of a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple porous animal living on the seabed, an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Reduction in sumptuous bonus

indicators.note: the word is reduced by losing its last letter

parts.note: plush means luxurious or sumptuous

explanation.surface: A cut in a lavish executive bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction in' clips the final H from PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or extra benefit, a synonym for a bonus.

clue.text: Expert adopting fashion immediately

indicators.note: the expert takes in, or adopts, the other word, so it is a container

parts.note: an ace is an expert
the ton is an old word for high fashion or the fashionable set

explanation.surface: An expert takes up a new fashion straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' is the container signal. 'Ton' for fashion is an old usage, as in the bon ton of Regency society.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-word phrase meaning straight away, without delay.

clue.text: Adverse cold weather event beginning to separate new head from spring flower

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used
the head, or first letter, is taken away from the flower

parts.note: the cowslip is a yellow spring-flowering primula

explanation.surface: A cold snap stops a spring flower from heading out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes one letter of 'separate'; 'head from' strips the opening letter of the flower. The surface hints at frost nipping a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small avalanche of snow sliding downhill, a hazard in cold weather.

clue.text: Second-placed team with some beef

parts.note: silver is the medal for coming second
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The runners-up team is served a portion of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: SILVERSIDE is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter, often salted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the outer thigh, so an example of some beef.

clue.text: Suggestion for positive redevelopment of Laos

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

indicators.note: redeveloping something rebuilds it in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A plan proposing a positive rebuilding of Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redevelopment of' rearranges LAOS into OSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, a suggestion.

clue.text: Quick move beginning to seem more theatrical?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly theatrical, so camper is more so

explanation.surface: A sudden dash starts to look rather overdramatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes the S of 'seem'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamper is a quick, light run, so a fast movement.

clue.text: Use of colour not good for cartoon character

indicators.note: the named letter is to be left out

parts.note: tinting is applying colour

explanation.surface: Applying colour, not good enough, to a cartoon figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the final G of TINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy reporter of Hergé's Belgian comic strips is a famous cartoon hero.

clue.text: African country's former currency

definitions.meaning: a West African nation with its capital at Conakry
an old British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings

explanation.surface: An African nation's old money.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves both the West African state and the old British coin of 21 shillings.

clue.text: Oscillation strength: average

parts.note: sinew means physical strength
AVE is the abbreviation for average

explanation.surface: A wobble of middling power.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth periodic curve describing a regular oscillation in physics.

clue.text: Feature of boat vendor brings in sailors to support

indicators.note: the seller takes the other pieces inside, so this is a container

parts.note: a vendor is a seller
a crew is the sailors on a ship
to prop is to support

explanation.surface: A boat salesman takes on sailors to back him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings in' is the container signal: the vendor's word is split after its first letter to take both inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating bladed device that drives a ship is a part of the vessel.

clue.text: Is it involving candle hire?

indicators.note: involving can mean entangling or twisting together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question whether renting candles is part of the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' rearranges CANDLE HIRE; the whole clue then asks whether the answer involves candles, which a traditional one does.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging light fitting with branches, traditionally holding candles.

clue.text: Regular payments low but rising, showing enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, buying through regular instalments
to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: Monthly instalments are modest but going up, which sounds keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns HPMOO upwards. 'showing' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour and energetic spirit, synonymous with zest or enthusiasm.

clue.text: He avoids pounds in quantity

indicators.note: the named letters stay away, i.e. are taken out

parts.note: pounds means crushes or mashes

explanation.surface: A man steers clear of a large amount of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like money but is the verb: MASHES, with 'avoids' removing HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a large amount or quantity of something.

clue.text: Famous actor was seen around right film

parts.note: a star is a famous actor

indicators.note: the word goes round the letter, so it is a container

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor was spotted near the right movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R inside WAS to give WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas's 1977 space-opera movie, one example of a film.

clue.text: One who'd link love with Italian city

definitions.text: One who'd link love with Italian city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: Someone who would join romance with an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads both ways: the letters join O to ROME, and Shakespeare's lover linked love with Verona, an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's lover in Verona, whose name now stands for any ardent suitor.

clue.text: Most unctuous love stories will be found in it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O

indicators.note: the stories are placed inside the following word, a container

parts.note: stories can mean fibs, i.e. lies

explanation.surface: The smarmiest love stories will be located in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be found in' is the container; 'love' is the tennis zero placed in front, not part of the surface's romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily describes a smarmy, ingratiating manner, so its superlative means most unctuous.

clue.text: Old man elected torture?

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, i.e. pa
a party elected is in power

explanation.surface: Was the old fellow voted in a form of torment?
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering, physical or mental, which torture is meant to inflict.

clue.text: Badly jolt the reader with note such as this?

definitions.text: Badly jolt the reader with note such as this?

indicators.note: the words are treated badly, i.e. mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A letter that badly shocks its reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges JOLT THE READER with N; the whole clue describes a letter breaking off a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter from a partner ending the relationship, which would certainly jolt its recipient.

clue.text: Propel boat, chasing vessel in Northern town

indicators.note: the piece chasing comes behind the other

parts.note: a jar is a container, or vessel
to row is to propel a boat with oars

explanation.surface: Rowing after a ship to reach a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: JARROW is a town in north-east England known for the 1936 Jarrow March.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Tyne in north-east England, so a northern town.

clue.text: Lights positioned around theatre, uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means reading upwards
one word goes around the other

parts.note: sat means placed or positioned
rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Lamps set around a theatre, a cheering sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' builds SREPAT; 'uplifting' looks like praise but in a down clue means the result is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapers are thin candles or wicks used to light, or as, lights.

clue.text: Antiquated dispute recalled in Lords by first of officials

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used
the reversed dispute sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: LD is the abbreviation for Lord, doubled for the plural as pp is for pages

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: An outdated quarrel brought back into the House of Lords by a senior official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives WOR, which goes 'in' the doubled abbreviation for Lords; 'first of officials' supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-world means quaint and belonging to the past, i.e. antiquated.

clue.text: Have calming effect on power-crazed uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up means read from the bottom

parts.note: mad means crazed

explanation.surface: Calming a power-crazed rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns PMAD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp, as in damp down, is to subdue or calm something.

clue.text: Pale rocks, very large, back in US city

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are rearranged
the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, i.e. very large

explanation.surface: Pale, very large rocks are returned to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges PALE to ELPA; 'back' turns OS into SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in western Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Evidence of wound a source of alarm? Not entirely

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: a scare is a fright, a source of alarm

explanation.surface: Is a wound's mark cause for alarm? Not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the final E of SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on the skin after a wound heals is evidence of it.

clue.text: Eccentric party located behind dam

indicators.note: the party comes after the dam

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An odd party held just past the dam.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd or unconventional person, used here as a noun for an oddball.

clue.text: Chap endlessly cuddling a bird like his mother?

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps round the others like a hug
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a male is a man or chap
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A man cuddling a bird in the way his mother might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves MAL, which 'cuddling' wraps round the bird with its article. The question mark flags that a man being motherly is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maternal means motherly, of or like a mother.
